items.impact: Crew-board records can contain task content, file paths, sender identity, and read receipts, but this window defines no audience authorization, redaction, sensitivity classification, tenant or workspace boundary, or auditable deletion rule. A builder must invent security and lifecycle policy for potentially sensitive coordination data.
items.statement: The crew-board data model stores full message content and per-agent read state without a normative privacy, authorization, or data-lifecycle contract in the assigned unit.
items.title: Crew-board message data lacks a security and lifecycle boundary

items.impact: A compromised, mistaken, or lower-authority child can place instructions in message content that are interpolated into another agent's prompt. No trust labeling, escaping, provenance boundary, content-size limit, or instruction-isolation oracle is specified, so cross-agent prompt injection can alter downstream execution.
items.statement: The prompt formatter directly interpolates crew-board message content into agent prompts without defining an untrusted-data boundary or a falsifiable sanitization and provenance contract.
items.title: Crew messages form an unguarded cross-agent prompt-injection channel

evidence.exact_quote: The supported v1 bound is up to 32 active agents across worktrees; above that, admission policy must queue or throttle new child runs.
**Size limits:** Limit coordination state to max 100 active agents. If exceeded, prune oldest agents (by `started_at`).

items.impact: One implementation can queue at 32 while another admits up to 100 and silently prunes live records. Pruning active agents would erase conflict and supervision visibility, while the same document requires admission control above 32.
items.statement: The assigned unit specifies mutually incompatible scale behavior: queue or throttle above 32 active agents, yet also admit a 100-agent state and prune the oldest records.
items.title: Coordination overflow is specified as both admission control and destructive pruning

items.impact: Any projection read error becomes indistinguishable from an empty conflict set, allowing parallel dispatch when file claims are unknown. This can authorize conflicting edits precisely during storage or projection failure.
items.statement: Conflict detection discards coordination-snapshot read errors with `.ok()` and then reports no file conflicts when the projection is unavailable.
items.title: Conflict detection fails open when coordination state cannot be read

evidence.exact_quote: Platform capability handling is provider-first, is limited to PM-supported runtime surfaces, and uses three execution classes:
All subagent work executes through provider CLI commands. Determinism comes from explicit args/env plus normalized event parsing from CLI output.

items.impact: Direct-provider and server-bridge implementations cannot satisfy a universal CLI execution rule. Builders can either violate the transport taxonomy or incorrectly wrap non-CLI providers, producing incompatible runtime and evidence behavior.
items.statement: The platform section defines direct, CLI-bridged, and server-bridged execution classes but later states that all subagent work executes through provider CLI commands.
items.title: Universal CLI execution conflicts with the three-class transport taxonomy

items.impact: A failed or incomplete phase inspection can still transition the orchestrator to the next phase. The advertised three-tier QA gate therefore does not enforce phase completion and can mark invalid work as advanced.
items.statement: The phase-inspector result is assigned but never evaluated before `advance_phase()` is called, both in the phase-completion sketch and the enhanced loop.
items.title: Phase advancement bypasses the phase-inspector verdict

items.impact: Producers and consumers can serialize different parent-attempt fields, and one required lineage field is absent from the earlier minimum projection list. This can break remediation correlation, artifact navigation, retry suppression, and recovery after restart.
items.statement: The runtime-field list names `remediation_parent_attempt_id`, while the later canonical remediation model requires `parent_attempt_id` and adds `remediation_generation` without resolving aliases or migration behavior.
items.title: Remediation lineage fields drift within the canonical runtime contract

items.impact: Critical claims such as pre-dispatch authority clamping, self-dispatch-loop rejection, parent-only clarification, hidden-channel prevention, capability-boundary enforcement, and timeout-token retirement can all remain unverified while generic migration validators pass.
items.statement: OSI-009 through OSI-015 use the same source-preservation and no-build-task acceptance template, with no unit-specific executable oracle for their authority, delegation, escalation, propagation, selection, or timeout requirements.

segments.summary: Reviewed cross-provider coordination, crew ownership and caps, crew enhancements, crew-board architecture, routing, and message data fields. The strongest adversarial gap is the absence of a normative privacy and audience-authorization boundary for rich coordination records.

Reviewed message routing, lifecycle, canonical append and projection APIs, prompt formatting, monitoring, rate and archive mitigations, and canonical versus mirror recovery. Direct interpolation of agent-authored content into prompts creates an unguarded cross-agent instruction channel.

Reviewed validation, crash recovery, file-operation inference, scale bounds, prompt truncation, file claims, path normalization, ingestion fallback, metrics, backup and schema migration sketches. The 32-agent admission bound conflicts with a 100-agent destructive-pruning mitigation.

Reviewed parallel isolation, conflict detection, concurrency ownership, provider capability classes, invocation selection, capability snapshots, and QA-loop introduction. Found a fail-open snapshot read in conflict detection and a universal CLI statement that contradicts the direct, CLI-bridge, and server-bridge taxonomy.

Reviewed progress selection, preflight, task and phase inspectors, pause behavior, commit rework, the enhanced loop, configuration, plan-graph change history, and Persona compatibility setup. Phase-inspector output is ignored before phase advancement, defeating the phase gate.

Reviewed Persona resolution, scheduler readiness, waits, wake cascades, retry and blocked taxonomy, remediation lineage, same-cycle scheduling, consumer projection fields, and the retired residual PlanUnit. Remediation parent-attempt field names and required lineage members drift within the unit.

Reviewed OSI-002 through OSI-008 and every field in their PlanUnit blocks. Their canonical statements are distinct, but their repeated acceptance template validates migration preservation rather than each unit's behavior or negative constraints.

Reviewed OSI-009 through OSI-015 and every field in their PlanUnit blocks. Their authority, delegation, escalation, propagation, selection, and timeout constraints have only generic source-preservation acceptance checks and therefore remain unfalsifiable.
